captionHtml:
This is me on my way up the hospital elevator. I had been out getting the camera when Julie called and said You better get to the hospital...NOW.

So here I am riding up the elevator on my way to go see my kids get born.
You may not be able to tell here, but Julie is in pain. At this point, she's been having contractions all morning, and she'll be wheeled away into the OR within five or ten minutes.

We're moments away from going into the OR (Operating Room for you med-school dropouts), so they made me put on this space suit with the funny hat and the booties over my shoes.

It was really hot wearing all this extra clothing (over my actual normal-daily-garb). Rumor has it that some people save their OR scrubs for future Halloween costumes, but I'll stick to monsters and whatnot.
They're wheeling Julie's bed out the OR. You can almost hear the Star Wars Imperial March theme music playing in the background.

This is a picture of Chloe just moments after she was born. Of course, she didn't actually have a name at this point. She was just BABY A or Smith Girl.

She cried when she was born (unlike her brother), and she got an APGAR score of 7 out of 10. Essentially, that means that she was exhibiting most of the signs of a healthy baby. Very impressive for someone born 3 months early.

This is julie about an hour or so after she finished birthing the twins. Doesn't she look fantastic?

Don't be fooled, though. She's about as loopy as a flock of pigeons and can hardly tell you her own name.

The loopiness is largely the result of the epidural that they gave her. She actually didn't want any anesthesia, but the doctor insisted. He said that if there was an emergency while delivering baby A (Chloe), then they would have to perform a C-section, in which case, they would want her to have already been anesthetized.

Consequently, loopiness...

If you

e ever in Provo and looking for a really cool place to eat, the Bombay House is it. We had our wedding dinner there.

captionHtml:
This is a picture of Chloe just moments before having eye surgery. They had to take all of the tubes off of her face, so they thought it would be a good time for a picture.

But, with her eyes dialated, she wasn't crazy about the flash going off.

Julie is getting ready to nurse Chloe.

Check out the next picutre to see her ACTUALLY NURSING CHLOE ON CAMERA!!!

Julie is nursing Chloe.

This was the only picture I was allowed to take.

These are the little containers of milk that Julie produces every three hours.

We have to make each container with a sticker for the kids and the date and time of pumping.

We currently have hundreds of these little containers in a cold-storage facility that we've rented

The purpose of this picture is to show all of the wires that were constantly connected to the kids. It was really difficult to do anything with all those wires around.

Plus, since we would get the kids out at different times, Owen's wires were constantly getting twisted around Chloe's wires (and vice versa).

On a couple of occasions, I tripped over the wires and brought some of their equipment crashing to the ground (those two boxes on the left-hand side of the picture, with the green and pink stickers).

This is one of my favorite pictures of the twins, up to this point.

You can only wonder, what is Owen doing in there?

This is what we lovingly refer to as Owen's happy Buddah face.

Could there possibly be a happier Buddah?

In fact, we're thinking of having a big statue carved of Owen, based on this photograph.

Poor little Chloe just had surgerey the day before (I think) this photo was taken.

The bump on the top of her head is where they placed the valve for the shunt. Through that valve is a tube that goes into the ventricles of her brain, and the other side of the tube goes down the right side of her head (the left side in the picture), back behind her ear, and into her abdomen, where the cerebrospinal fluid is absorbed into her bloodstream.

She's kind of zoned out in this picutre. She wasn't too happy.
This is the day Owen was officially paroled from the hospital. If he keeps up his good behavior, we hope we can keep him out of the hooskow for at least a few more years.

At this point, Owen is still little enough that he'll tip right over in his swing without bumpers on both sides of him. So, we've rolled up a couple of blankets to help keep him in place.

He seems very snug and happy.

Having Owen at home has generated an unprecedented amount of laundry.

When Chloe comes home, Julie and I are going to stop wearing clothes, to facilitate the fact that these kids can destroy three different outfits in a single day.

For some reason, Owen really likes to get his hair washed with this scratchy sponge.

Honestly, I probably could have kept washing his hair for twenty minutes, and he wouldn't have put up a fuss at all. He really likes it.

Owen is in the laundry basket.

I don't know why.

But I suppose it's funny to put babies into funny places. Perhaps we'll take a picture next week with Owen in a dresser drawer. Or Owen in the trunk of the car. Or Owen in the fireplace.

This a picutre of my (Benji's) mom after she's had a day or so to meet Owen.

They've had lots of fun. They went on a walk, and she helped give him a bath. And she hugs him and kisses him (a lot).

This is a picture of Chloe right after her second shunt-placement surgery. You can see the place on her tummy where they made an incision to place the downstream-end of the tube.

And she's got a little splint on her right arm to keep her from bending her wrist, where they put in an IV.

The cloth over her face is to protect her eyes from the brightness of the lights in the NICU at Primary Children's Medical Center (in Salt Lake, where they performed the surgery), since her eyes were still kind of weird from the anesthesia.

You can see the bump on Chloe's head really clearly in this photo.

The bump is actually a little plastic valve that they put in under her scalp. The valve is attached to her skull, and there is a little plastic tube going through it. The upstream-end of the tube goes into her brain (into the ventricles), and the downstream-end drains into her abdomen.

This little bump will be there the rest of her life (but when she's bigger and has hair, no one will ever notice).
If I'm not mistaken, this photo was taken shortly after Chloe was transported back down to Utah Valley Regional Medical Center (in Provo) after having her second brain surgery (in Salt Lake).

This is a great shot showing the results of Chloe's shunt-placement surgery.

What looks like a big thick vein running down the side of her head and behind her ear is actually the shunt tube. In diameter, it's about the same size as the tubes that have been going down her nose and into her stomach.

The slimy ooze on top of her head is actually just some Neosporin to help her heal from her incision.

If you look closely at the slimy spot, you can actually see her stitches. Cool!

This is my mom. She was positively thrilled to come out and see the kids.

Chloe seems to like her.

My mom cuddles with Owen.

He starts to get antsy.

He starts to fuss.

You can see the beginnings of a really good cry welling up here.

You can see the shape of my mom's lips making a 'shhh' sound.

check out the next photo

The fussing progresses.

check out the next photo

Full-scale pandemonium.

My mom starts to lose her cool.

After this photo is snapped, she tells me to delete it.

No way.

check out the next photo

Ten minutes have passed.

A calm settles over the household.

Owen is cheery.

My mom is relieved.

...And they lived happily ever after.

I don't know why this picture is in here, or even why it was taken. But it's such a captivating picture that I decided to keep it.

Just look at those eyes. They're piercing, aren't they?

This is Julie's mom. She came to visit us for a week, after my mom left, to help us take care of Owen.

Lately, Owen has been treated with the fantastic mental imagery of master storyteller J. K. Rowling.

Julie has been reading him Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. We've got to get Owen caught up. He's way behind. Book 5 in the series comes out in only two months, and Owen has to read all four of the preceding books.

That explains the look of disconcernment that you can see on his face in this shot.

READ FASTER, MOM!

After a hard day of quilting and churning butter, Owen is usually pretty exhausted, so we let him unwind with a nice warm bottle of breastmilk.

In this photo, Owen has been falling asleep in the middle of his feeding, so we've had to put a cool wet washcloth on his head to try to wake him up.

For my 25th birthday, Julie and I went to The Melting Pot in downtown SLC. It\'s a fondue restaurant, so all of your food needs to be dipped-in-something before you eat it. Raw meat needs to be dipped into a boiling broth/wine mixture for a minute or two to cook. Veggies and bread get dipped in molten cheese. And strawberries and cheesecake get dipped in thick creamy chocolate.

It was a nice birthday dinner.

We spent about 80% of our San Francisco vacation sitting in a bus or a subway car. Generally, by the time we finally got somewhere, we realized that we didn't have enough time to take public transit BACK to wherever it was that we wanted to be next. On one occasion, we arrived at our chosen restaurant, sat down to eat, and realized that if we were going to make it to the theatre in time for the evening's entertainment, we would have to get back on a bus RIGHT NOW. So we walked right out of the restaurant without so much as a sip of water. The chef followed us out into the street (it was a tiny, personable French restaurant) and asked us why we didn't want to stay. It was very embarrasing.

Anyhow, in this picutre we're leaving the Golden Gate Bridge. Apparantly, it closes at sunset. We spent like 20 minutes there.

The moral of the story: if you're going to San Francisco, RENT A CAR.

titleHtml: Why is Mom happy when baby is sad?
titleText: Why is Mom happy when baby is sad?
captionHtml: That's the question mankind has been asking itself for ages.

The thing about these pictures is that you probably assume we (the parents) are setting them up.

"Wouldn't it be funny if we put oxygen tubes all over Owen's face!!!"

But, actually, Owen does it himself. I usually only take candid shots, so anything crazy that you see Owen do was probably his own idea.

In this case, Owen was having a blast playing with the tubes on his face, so we took a picture of it.

Our house has been utterly overtaken by electrical/medical stuff. Which is odd, because we only have 2 kids, and neither one of them is on any sort of constant life support stuff.

The plastic tubing belongs to Owen. There is only one tube (it's for his oxygen) but it's like 60 feet long (so that we can take him anywhere in the house). So, even though there's only one tube, it seems like there are hundreds of them everywhere.

As for the electrical wiring, I think that's just because A) It's summer and it's hot and we have fans everywhere. and B) We live in a 75-year-old house with very few electrical outlets, so we have extension cords everywhere.

Every time we take a picture of Owen with something crazy on his head, it's his own doing. We never pose these pictures. They're 100% reality.

So the fact that Owen has a toy on his face in this picture simply means that Owen likes to have toys on his face.

This is how Owen sleeps every night lately, curled up into the corner. Although, in this picture, he appears to be afraid that the bed will tip over, since he's hanging on for dear life.

Often, he ends up on his stomach by the time we wake him up for his next feeding. And if he's already mad, being stuck on his stomach doesn't help much.

If we could just convince him to sleep on his back...
Chloe loves her daddy.  She also loves being tickled.
Chloe trying to hold her head up-it is very heavy!
Benji and Casey catch a cat nap.
Both Chloe and Owen love this green metallic paper.

captionHtml: Almost every picture of them together on the floor is of Owen trying to get Chloe.  Some day she will fight back!  Go girl.
This is what Julie does all day-consols one while trying to keep the other one happy.
I love my beans and rice!
Here Chloe is being forced to sit in the beans and rice.  According to her Occupational Therapist, it is good for her balance, but if you ask Chloe....
If we give her enough choices, she is bound to like something, right??
We are twins.  See how we like to pester each other?
Get off of my blankie!!!
Here Owen is experimenting to see if his sleep is more restful if his arms are twisted up.
Julie looking freaked out at her birthday dinner at the Melting Pot.
Here Benji and Julie celebrate the many hours of labor that Jean underwent 29 years ago.   Thanks Mom!!
Ain't he cute?
Just a little more to the left....
Owen likes to chew on Zwieback toast, but only in the nude.
What happened to my top half?
Chloe during dinner-she was giggling right before the picture took-I swear.
There is something to be said for big head size.  Consequently, Owen is very smart.
You can't tell because this is only a picture, but here Owen is singing.  It sounds a bit like a siren.  He's so talented!!
Three times a month a vison therapist comes and tortures Chloe.  Her name is Terri.  She is very good and Chloe is getting better all the time.  Torture works!
Owen likes this little pumpkin that shakes when you pull the cord in the back.
Where did my pupils go?
Chloe just finished her bath and life is good.
Happy Halloween from Owen the friendly Clown.
Pillows help us sit up so that Mom can take pictures of us.  We like it.
Owen wants out of there and Chloe thinks her hat doesn't fit right.
Now Chloe wants out.  That pumpkin is poison!
Who can work in these conditions?  Where's my make up guy?
Owen thinks that if he could only get that stem off, then he could eat it.
That really is only Julie's hair hanging down, not rays of light coming out of Chloe's mouth.
We gave up on the hat.
Now that the lights are out, she can finally relax.
I am soooo cool. Nevermind all of these lousy baby photos. Check me out. Yeah.

Just look at this guy and TELL ME you don't see a little bit of his face in Chloe and Owen.

PLEASE tell me you don't see his face in Chloe and Owen.

[NOTE TO MICHAEL: Just Kidding.]

Owen got himself into this mess. First he climbed up into the swing. And then, deciding that he didn't have enough toys to play with, he pulled up the keyboard.

Now he's trapped.
Now he realizes that he's trapped.
